newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares backtrack after breaking records.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares backtrack after breaking records.

text.p: European shares backtracked on Tuesday after roaring to new record trading highs in early business, encouraged by another closing peak on Wall Street, its 14th this year.
However, the Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue chip shares was up just eight points by the end of European business on Tuesday, with weaker bonds holding prices back.

London's FTSE index shot to a new high of 4,466.3 within minutes of opening, beating the previous all-time peak of 4,440.8 set on Monday. But a few doubts about the Dow halted the advance and it closed up 6.9 points at 4,444.3 -- though this was still its sixth consecutive record close.
"We got another big boost from the Street this morning but some people are asking how long that can continue," one London dealer said.
"But people have been calling the top for Wall Street for some time and it keeps confounding expectations."
Dealers reported good two-way business, with profit-taking hitting some stocks as they reached higher levels but enough investors buying stock to keep the market firm.
"We have seen a bit of profit-taking in places but it's been outweighed by good buying interest," the dealer said. "The prevailing opinion is that the market still has further to go."
European bourses received an early boost from the Dow, which jumped 78 points on Monday.

The London market was also helped by positive reaction to blue-chip annual results and a more optimistic view of Britain's interest rate outlook following Monday's comments by Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
The bulls were firmly in charge on the German share market, where the DAX index surged in bourse trade to end the session at its second record close in a row.
The DAX ended up 24.52 points at 3,460.59, having earlier hit a record intraday high of 3,474.98. Dealers said a breach of its next key resistance level at 3,500 was on the cards.

"We will see 3,500." said a Frankfurt dealer, who said he was taken aback by the pace of the market's advance, despite continued solid earnings signals for German firms from the strong dollar. "If this goes on much longer, we'll be at 4,000."
But French shares ended lower after a gust of profit-taking took the Paris bourse lower in late afternoon.
Traders said a slip in the dollar versus the mark, later corrected, sent a signal for investors to book profits on some of the market's recent strong rise.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 23.06 points or 0.85 percent at 2,686.15.
The dollar closed at around 1.7035 marks, little changed from its late level in Europe on Monday, after a rally against the mark fizzled out.
It remained supported by buoyant U.S. asset markets, however, and receding fears about a delay to the start of European economic and monetary union (EMU), traders said.
The U.S. currency found solid bids on a dip below 1.70 marks and sentiment remained bullish after Wall Street closed at a fresh record on Monday and made another firm start on Tuesday.

"The dollar is rangebound but there's a feeling that there's more upside to come so it's really well supported on dips," said a senior trader at a German bank here. "It's just taking a breather after its rise above 1.72 marks on Friday."
Comments on Tuesday by Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler, that there was no case for a German interest rate move up or down, failed to move the dollar.
News that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had reshuffled his cabinet prompted limited kneejerk dollar buying against the mark but had little net effect.
Support for the mark ebbed further after a slew of comments from Bundesbank council members that the single European currency should be launched on time.

"The economic fundamentals and interest rate outlook as well as the strength of the Dow still all point to a higher dollar, while the Bundesbank are clearly now acting together to calm market fears of an EMU delay," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London.

The dollar recovered from an overnight low at 121.25 yen, hit on news of a robust 11.8 percent rise in Japanese machinery orders in January and after the benchmark three-month certificate of deposit rate rose to 0.55 percent, the highest since last August. It stood at 121.75 yen in late trade.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7035 marks and 121.75 yen compared with 1.7027 and 121.74 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.9 points at 4,444.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 23.06 points at 2,686.15.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 24.52 points at 3,460.59 points. In post-bourse electronic trading the Ibis DAX was up 4.18 points at 3,430.95.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $351.95 an ounce after closing at $350.75 in London on Monday.
